title: Quarterly vs. Annual Calendar for Tile and Grout Deep Cleaning: Frequency by Foot Traffic & Annual Spend
seoTitle: Quarterly Annual Calendar Tile and Grout Deep Cleaning: Spend Guide
metaDescription: Quarterly annual calendar tile and grout deep cleaning: match monthly, quarterly, or yearly scrubs to foot traffic at $0.75–$1.25/sq ft. Try the calculator.
excerpt: Foot traffic, not habit, should decide whether your office tile gets deep scrubbed monthly, quarterly, or once a year. This guide gives traffic thresholds, a sample 12-month calendar, and the annualized cost of each schedule.
quickAnswer: Low-traffic office tile (under 150 people per day crossing it) usually needs a deep scrub once a year, medium traffic (150–500 daily) quarterly, and heavy-traffic restrooms, lobbies, and cafes (500+ daily) monthly or every other month. At a typical $0.75–$1.25 per sq ft per scrub, 1,000 sq ft of tile costs roughly $750–$1,250 a year on an annual calendar, $3,000–$5,000 quarterly, and $9,000–$15,000 monthly.

blocks.text: Traffic Is the Variable That Sets the Calendar

Grout is a porous cement joint that sits slightly below the tile face. Every footstep carries grit and moisture that a damp mop pushes into that recess, and once soil compacts in the joint, routine mopping cannot reach it. How fast that happens depends on how many people cross the floor, what they track in, and whether the floor sees liquid spills. A facility manager who schedules grout scrubbing by headcount and soil source, rather than by a vendor's default package, typically spends less and gets more consistent appearance.

We use daily crossings, the number of people who walk across a given tiled zone per day, as the practical metric. An elevator lobby in a 400-person building may see 1,200 crossings a day; a private executive washroom may see 10.

blocks.title: Translate to the monthly budget line
blocks.text: Divide annual cost by 12. A quarterly program on 1,000 sq ft at $1.00 per sq ft costs $4,000 a year, or $333 per month. Our deep-floor benchmark of $0.03–$0.06 per sq ft per month applies to your whole floor plate, so on a 10,000 sq ft office this tile program alone would be $0.033 per sq ft per month.
A Sample 12-Month Calendar for a Mixed-Traffic Office

Most offices have more than one traffic tier. A 20,000 sq ft office with a 600 sq ft ground lobby, 1,200 sq ft of restrooms, and a 400 sq ft executive kitchenette should not put all three on the same interval. Staggering them also smooths cash flow and lets one crew mobilization cover multiple zones.

items: January: lobby and restrooms deep scrub (post-holiday salt and slush soil removal).
April: restrooms deep scrub plus penetrating sealer touch-up on worn traffic lanes.
July: lobby, restrooms, and annual executive kitchenette scrub combined in one visit.
November: lobby pre-winter scrub and full reseal before salt season.

blocks.text: At $1.00 per sq ft, that calendar costs 6 lobby visits times $600 ($3,600), 4 restroom visits times $1,200 ($4,800), and one kitchenette visit at $400, for $8,800 a year, or about $733 per month. Putting everything on a flat bimonthly schedule would cost $13,200, so traffic-matching saves about a third.
Seasonal and Site Conditions That Shorten Intervals

Snowbelt buildings see calcium and sodium chloride ice-melt tracked in from November through March; the white residue bonds to grout and accelerates darkening. Coastal and Sun Belt properties deal with sand and summer humidity that keep grout damp longer. Restrooms with urinals need shorter intervals regardless of headcount because uric salts crystallize in joints near fixtures and create persistent odor. If your building has any of these conditions, move one tier up from the headcount table.
Extending the Interval With Soil Control

Matting is the cheapest way to stretch the calendar. Industry rules of thumb hold that 12–15 feet of combined walk-off matting captures most tracked soil before it reaches tile. A corrugated ribbed rubber runner such as the Rubber-Cal 3x12 ft runner, 1/8 inch thick and non-slip, works well at wet service entries and dock doors where moisture is the problem. At security desks and reception counters on tile, a closed-cell nitrile mat like the Wearwell 24/7, 3x5 ft and 5/8 inch thick with beveled edges, protects the floor where staff stand for hours and reduces localized grout wear. Between scrubs, an EPA-registered disinfectant such as Lysol Professional Disinfectant Spray can be applied to restroom fixtures and high-touch points, but it is not a grout cleaner; disinfectants need clean surfaces and full label dwell time to work.

items.text: Align zones so every mobilization covers enough footage to exceed the vendor's $250–$450 minimum.

items.text: Photograph grout at each visit; if joints look clean at scrub time, extend that zone's interval.

blocks.title: Do not let intervals slip too far
blocks.text: Waiting 18–24 months on medium-traffic tile often pushes the next job from a maintenance scrub at $0.75–$1.25 per sq ft into restorative pricing at $1.25–$2.50, wiping out any savings from skipped visits.

faqs.q: Is quarterly tile and grout cleaning standard for offices?
faqs.a: Quarterly is the most common default because it fits medium-traffic restrooms and breakrooms, but it is not right for every zone. Low-traffic tile can go annual, and heavy lobbies may need bimonthly or monthly work. Ask vendors to price each zone individually instead of a single building-wide frequency.

faqs.q: How does deep scrub frequency interact with my weekly janitorial contract?
faqs.a: Routine contracts bill per visit times 4.333 weeks per month for weekly service. Deep scrubs are typically separate work orders. To compare total floor spend, convert deep scrubs to monthly by multiplying cost per visit by visits per year and dividing by 12, then add it to the routine monthly figure.

faqs.q: Should grout be resealed every time it is deep scrubbed?
faqs.a: No. A quality penetrating sealer generally lasts one to three years on office tile depending on traffic and cleaning chemistry. Reseal traffic lanes annually and full floors every two to three years, and have the vendor do a water-drop test to confirm when sealer has worn off.

faqs.q: What safety rules apply to scheduled grout scrubbing during business hours?
faqs.a: Wet tile is a slip hazard, so OSHA walking-working surface rules (29 CFR 1910.22) require keeping floors as dry as possible and marking wet areas. Daytime work should be cordoned with cones, and crews must have Safety Data Sheets on site under HazCom. Most offices schedule deep scrubs after hours to avoid these issues.
